title: Backport fixes to a release branch with git
prompt:
The current directory is a git repository (branch main, tag v1.0). Create the branch release-1.1, starting at the tag v1.0, that backports fixes from main:
- Take the commits of main after v1.0 (v1.0..main) whose subject starts with "fix:", oldest first, and cherry-pick each onto release-1.1, keeping its subject.
- Skip a fix whose subject contains "[no-backport]".
- Skip a fix that only changes files which do not exist at v1.0 (it fixes a feature that was never released).
- No merge commits; do not change main or the tag v1.0.

When you are done, release-1.1 must be checked out with a clean working tree. If git asks who you are, set user.name and user.email in this repository only (git config, without --global).
